title: Beyond the Gunshot: ShotSpotter Forensics in High-Profile Investigations
summary: A prosecutor, ATF veteran, and forensic lab director explain how ShotSpotter evidence supports charging decisions and courtroom testimony.
body_markdown:
Dooher walked through the kinds of questions a Detailed Forensic Report (DFR) is built to help answer once a case moves toward trial, several with real-world texture:


·


**Who fired first:** In multiple-shooter incidents, the DFR can assist in determining the sequence of shots fired from various locations — crucial evidence for self-defense claims. Dooher pointed out that this type of analysis is most effective when the shooters are significantly distanced from one another, rather than trying to differentiate shooters positioned at an arm’s length apart.


·


**Multiple firearms:** Overlapping audio, where shots register faster than a single firearm could be fired twice, can support expert testimony that more than one weapon was involved.


·


**Speed and direction of travel:** In true drive-by shootings, where a vehicle is moving while shots are fired, the acoustic data can help establish direction and speed of travel. A scenario where the vehicle stops before the shooter fires would not generate this kind of moving data.


·


**Cadence and pauses:** Often the sheer number of shots fired or the intervals between them powerfully demonstrate the shooter’s premeditation and deliberation. Pauses between successive bursts of gunfire can provide supporting evidence that the shooter either reloaded the weapon or encountered a firearm malfunction.


·


**Sensor participation:** Dooher described an intriguing case in which the final shot, amidst a series of many, was detected by only a few sensors in contrast to more than a dozen sensors that registered the previous shots. That distinction supported the prosecutor’s theory of an execution-style ending. A gunshot fired into the ground results in a significant portion of the sound waves being absorbed by the earth and the victim, resulting in a diminished detection range.


·


**Firing position and movement:** In one case Dooher prosecuted in Oakland, ShotSpotter data mapped a shooting that moved across roughly five to six city blocks as the defendant chased his victim on foot. The location analysis supported a premeditation and deliberation argument and corroborated the physical evidence.
